chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man had intercourse with a boy, is his sister permissible for him?' He said, 'If there was penetration, then no.'

key_terms.أَتَى: He had intercourse with / He went to
key_terms.ثَقَبَ: Penetration (specifically in the context of sexual intercourse)

ai.seo_question: Does a man's sexual intercourse with a boy make the boy's sister forbidden for him to marry?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that sexual intercourse with a boy constitutes a valid impediment for marriage to his sister, provided there was penetration (thaqaba), aligning with the principle of *kunya* (marriage by affinity). This ruling highlights the juristic consensus in Shia fiqh that the specific act of intercourse, rather than mere proximity, creates the prohibition, distinguishing it from other forms of affinity. The narration underscores the precision required in deriving legal consequences from specific physical acts in marital jurisprudence.
